title: Telemetry-driven version assertions & runtime semver policy
creator: Liam Chen
description: Implement a runtime semantic versioning policy that pairs traditional semver rules with runtime telemetry assertions. The goal is to minimize surprise for integrators while enabling safe iteration. This ticket designs the policy, required runtime signals, rollout gate thresholds, and a set of upgrade tooling (compat-checker + telemetry assertions) that together support safe LTS and non-LTS channels. Deliverables: policy doc, signal schema, compatibility test harness, and an RFC + reference implementation for the CLI migration assistant.
acceptance_criteria: Policy doc published in Confluence and linked from developer onboarding page
Runtime emits compatibility signals (compatibility.warn, compat.break, compat.metrics) in standard event format
compat-checker (CLI) can scan a recorded trace and surface potential breaking changes with severity scores
Canary rollout automation can consume signals and trigger automated rollbacks if thresholds breached
Integration tests demonstrate no silent regressions on three representative workloads (chat, embeddings, streaming)
risks: False positives from telemetry-driven assertions could block benign releases
Telemetry volume overhead impacting tail latency if signals are too verbose
Incomplete signal coverage (e.g., KV cache behavior or quantization artifacts) may miss real breakages
Operator confusion if policy messaging is ambiguous across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments
implementation_plan: Write semver policy doc that defines breaking-change taxonomy specific to runtime behavior (API wire schema, request semantics, response token ordering, streaming contract, cache/kv contract, kernel ABI behavior)
Design a compact runtime signal schema and low-overhead transport for compatibility events (batched, sampled)
Implement compatibility assertions in runtime: a) header-level response markers, b) periodic event stream for background analysis
Build compat-checker CLI to run on recorded traces / smoke tests and assign severity scores
Add contract tests to CI (unit + integration + smoke against pinned LTS images)
Hook signals into rollout automation (canary -> ramp -> full) with rollback thresholds for latency, error-rate, and eval-quality drift
Publish migration playbook targeted at dedicated/private customers with instructions for offline upgrades and KV cache migration steps
verification_plan: Create three test scenarios that exercise schema changes, streaming boundary shifts, and cache key semantics; run compat-checker and verify alerts
Deploy change behind a feature flag and run 1% canary for 24h; verify no compat.break events and <0.5% quality drift on eval harness
Simulate load to validate telemetry sampling keeps overhead <0.5% p99 latency
Run migration playbook in staging with partner account and document steps/time/expected rollback plan
notes: We intentionally define major-version triggers narrowly to allow behavioral opt-ins (feature flags) without forcing major bumps for performance or internal kernel improvements
Telemetry assertions are advisory by default; breaking signals escalate to enforced gating for LTS branches only
For private deployments we include an opt-in ‘strict-compat’ mode that enforces compat checks during upgrades
This ticket scopes the policy and reference tooling; full migration assistant integration into Console is a follow-up
